# 2026-10-30 recheck: Charlotte extension vote and NAACP v. X.AI Fifth Circuit order

Two due watchlist items (L038c, C28b). Sources were fetched with the summarizing fetch tool unless noted, so wording is paraphrase, not verbatim.

## L038c: Charlotte, NC moratorium extension (RESOLVED at article level)
- The city council voted on Monday Oct 26, 2026, to extend its data center moratorium by 11 months. Both WFAE (Oct 27) and WBTV (Oct 27) say the vote was unanimous; neither gives an exact count.
- New expiration: Oct 18, 2027. The prior pause (a 150-day moratorium approved unanimously Jun 8) was set to end Nov 5, 2026. A pre-vote GovTech piece said "through Oct 11, 2027", so the 10-11 date appears to be superseded; the city's official ordinance has not been read.
- Scope: halts acceptance, processing and approval of applications for new data centers inside city limits. WBTV says the language is similar to the first moratorium. Existing permits were unaffected under the first moratorium; WFAE repeats that existing permits are unaffected. Whether pre-extension approvals are exempt is not stated in the WBTV piece.
- Council stance (WFAE): it is waiting on the General Assembly to pass new laws early next session; District 6 member Kimberly Owens said the council had "no other option," citing state limits on downzoning (paraphrase of the article).
- Not found: exact vote count, the ordinance text, early-termination criteria.
- Sources: https://www.wfae.org/energy-environment/2026-10-27/charlotte-extends-its-data-center-moratorium-for-11-more-months ; https://www.wbtv.com/2026/10/27/data-center-moratorium-extended-city-charlotte-what-know/ (headline-level confirmation also from Bisnow and WUNC search results, not fetched).

## C28b: NAACP v. X.AI, Fifth Circuit No. 26-60806 (primary document read)
- Document: Fifth Circuit unpublished per curiam order filed Oct 19, 2026 (Stewart, Richman, Haynes), as hosted by Earthjustice; I extracted its text from the PDF.
- Posture: the movant-appellant is the United States, acting for the EPA Administrator; appellees are the NAACP and the Mississippi State Conference. Appeal from N.D. Miss., USDC No. 3:26-CV-74.
- Holding: the United States' opposed motion to stay the district court proceedings pending appeal was DENIED because the district court has not fully determined the issue; the motion can be refiled if the district court does not allow the United States to participate in a preliminary injunction. The court GRANTED motions by X.AI Corp./MZX Tech and by the State of Mississippi to file amicus briefs supporting the stay motion.
- This corrects the earlier watchlist wording ("no ruling found"): there is a ruling, and it is a denial without prejudice.
- Not found: whether the district court has since ruled on the United States' participation or on the NAACP's preliminary injunction request. District docket not checked.
- Source: https://earthjustice.org/document/motion-for-a-stay-denied-naacp-v-xai (PDF text read locally).
